faq.q: What is the origin of Essa?
faq.a: Essa is associated with Hebrew. Variant romanization of عيسى, the Qur'anic name of Jesus. The source record's gloss 'The Messiah, Jesus Christ' is a reasonable rendering.
No — the underlying form is Hebrew, not Arabic.
Essa can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Hebrew-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Essa should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. عيسى is named in the Qur'an (e.g. 3:45)

faq.a: No verified Persian form was established for Essa.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Essa, essa. Script forms are عيسى, عیسی, عیسیٰ, ईसा.

faq.q: Is Essa a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
